info.title: Shots API
info.description:
Shots turns a software release into a reviewed launch: a cited brief, on-brand visuals, and channel posts that a person approves before anything is scheduled. This API exposes the same workspace operations the app uses.

## Quickstart

1. Create a workspace API key in **Settings → Developer API** (`https://shots.playbookmedia.io/settings/developers`). Give it only the scopes it needs. The key is shown once.
2. Send it in the `X-API-Key` header:

```bash
export SHOTS_API_KEY="ss_..."
curl https://shots.playbookmedia.io/api/v1/releases -H "X-API-Key: $SHOTS_API_KEY"
```

3. Create a draft campaign. Every post starts as a draft; nothing is scheduled until a person approves it:

```bash
curl -X POST https://shots.playbookmedia.io/api/v1/campaigns \
  -H "X-API-Key: $SHOTS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: recurring-invoices-launch" \
  -d '{"name":"Recurring invoices","objective":"Announce recurring invoices","posts":[{"channel":"linkedin","copy":"Recurring invoices are here."}]}'
```

4. Submit the drafts for review with `POST /api/v1/campaigns/{campaignId}/review-requests`. Approvers decide in the app.

### Publish a post

With a key that holds `post:publish`, one call writes a post and schedules or publishes it. No key has that scope unless someone chose it.

1. Find the accounts with `GET /api/v1/social-sets`. Each account's `id` is what you post to. A key sees shared social sets only.
2. To attach media, call `POST /api/v1/assets/upload-url`, `PUT` the bytes to the returned URL with `If-None-Match: *`, then call `POST /api/v1/assets/{assetId}/complete`.
3. Publish:

```bash
curl -X POST https://shots.playbookmedia.io/api/v1/posts \
  -H "X-API-Key: $SHOTS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: launch-post-recurring-invoices" \
  -d '{"channelConnectionIds":["cl..."],"posts":[{"text":"Recurring invoices are here."}],"publishNow":true}'
```

Say when with exactly one of `publishNow`, `scheduledFor`, `localTime` with `timeZone`, and `queue`. Two or more `posts` make a thread. `platforms` sets one platform's own text and settings, such as a LinkedIn `firstComment`. Read each account's outcome with `GET /api/v1/content-drafts/{id}/posts`.

A workspace that requires approval keeps that rule: the draft is created, nothing is queued, and `status` is `awaiting_approval`.

### Typed TypeScript client

The document is OpenAPI 3.1. Generate types from it and call the API with full request and response typing:

```bash
npx openapi-typescript https://shots.playbookmedia.io/openapi.json -o shots.d.ts
npm install openapi-fetch
```

```ts
import createClient from 'openapi-fetch'
import type { paths } from './shots'

const shots = createClient<paths>({
  baseUrl: 'https://shots.playbookmedia.io',
  headers: { 'X-API-Key': process.env.SHOTS_API_KEY! },
})
const { data, error } = await shots.GET('/api/v1/campaigns/{campaignId}', {
  params: { path: { campaignId: 'c...' } },
})
```

## Authentication

| Credential | How to send it | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace API key | `X-API-Key: ss_...` | Scripts, CI, and agents. A key belongs to one workspace and carries scopes. |
| Signed-in session | The `better-auth.session_token` cookie | Same-origin browser calls, checked against the member's role. |

Each operation lists the scope it needs in its security requirement. A key can never choose another workspace: the workspace is the key's own.

| Scope | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `artifact:read` | Read releases, campaigns, the review queue, the publishing schedule, and link previews; sign asset downloads; use the editor utilities. |
| `asset:write` | Complete and delete asset uploads. |
| `draft:comment` | Add, reply, edit your own comments, and resolve discussions on workspace drafts. Never approves or publishes. |
| `draft:write` | Create, update, and delete content drafts. Posting to your accounts takes its own scope. |
| `onboarding:run` | Read a product site into its profile and follow the run. |
| `post:publish` | Write and publish new posts to the accounts of your shared social sets, right away or at a time, with no review by a person unless the workspace requires approval. Cancelling them takes the scheduling scope too. |
| `post:schedule` | Schedule campaign posts and visuals a person approved, and cancel scheduled posts. It never approves anything. |
| `queue:write` | Change future posting-slot suggestions and time zones. Does not approve, schedule, or move existing posts. |
| `release:create` | Create releases and draft campaigns, and submit drafts for review. |
| `source:write` | Register and update release-intake sources. |
| `upload:sign` | Sign asset uploads. |

Approving, rejecting, or requesting changes on posts is a person's decision and takes a session only. Those operations refuse API keys with `403`, whatever the key's scopes.

A key with `post:schedule` may schedule campaign posts and visuals a person approved, and cancel scheduled posts. A key with the separate `post:publish` scope may write and publish new posts with `POST /api/v1/posts`, with no review unless the workspace requires approval. A stored content draft is scheduled by a person, whatever the key's scopes. A session that schedules a variant or cancels a post needs a sign-in under 15 minutes old with two-factor enabled.

Shell operations (`/api/v1/me`, `/api/v1/bootstrap`, `/api/v1/organizations`) describe the signed-in user and refuse API keys.

## Plans and limits

There is no free plan: every operation here needs a Pro, Business or Enterprise subscription, and a workspace without one can only sign in and choose a plan. Each gated operation publishes its gate in `x-shots-entitlement`: the `feature` it needs, the `minimumPlan` that includes it, and the `quota` it consumes.

- A workspace without the feature gets `403` with code `workspace_feature_not_entitled`, plus `feature`, `currentPlan`, and `requiredPlan`.
- A metered write past its quota gets `429` with code `workspace_quota_exceeded`, plus `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` headers.
- Each API key is also limited to 60 requests per minute.

## Idempotency

Creating a release, campaign, or scheduled post accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header of up to 128 characters. `POST /api/v1/posts` requires one of 16 to 128. A retry with the same key returns the original result with `200` instead of creating a duplicate. Status changes (campaign transitions, review requests, approvals, cancellations) apply only from the current status, so a repeated request returns `409` and changes nothing.

## Errors

Every failure returns one JSON envelope with a stable `code`, a human-readable `message`, and a `hint`. Branch on `code`; it is stable within `v1`. Every response carries `X-Request-Id`; send your own to correlate logs.

post.description: Schedules an approved creative variant, or a content draft, to an active channel connection. Send exactly one of `variantId` and `contentDraftId`. A variant must be `APPROVED` with an approved review; scheduling never approves. Only a signed-in member schedules a content draft; an API key gets `403`. A key also sends only text a person approved: `caption` must be the copy of an approved campaign post for this visual, otherwise `403`. To post new text, use `POST /api/v1/posts`. A key cannot schedule to an account in a private social set. Everything must belong to the workspace. Each new post counts against the monthly posts allowance. Accepts `Idempotency-Key`, unique per channel connection: a retry returns the first post with `200`. Requires the `post:schedule` scope, or a member who manages publishing, signed in within 15 minutes with two-factor.

post.description: Writes a post or thread and schedules or publishes it to accounts of one shared social set, with no review by a person. Say when with exactly one of `publishNow`, `scheduledFor`, `localTime`, and `queue`. A workspace that requires approval keeps that rule: the draft is created, nothing is queued, and `status` is `awaiting_approval` with a `reviewPath`. Every check runs first, so a refused post leaves no draft. Each account's post counts against the monthly posts allowance. Requires `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key and content returns the first result with `200` and never posts twice. A published post can't be recalled by retrying, so read the post's status with `GET /api/v1/content-drafts/{id}/posts` rather than posting again. Requires the `post:publish` scope, which no key has unless someone chose it.

post.description: Adds, replies, edits, deletes or resolves a comment on a visible draft. Every active member may comment; only its author may edit a comment, while owners/admins may also delete comments. Author identities and timestamps are server-owned. A new thread may include anchor {platform, postId, quote?}; quote must match exactly once in the selected post. Omit quote to discuss the whole post. delete_thread removes a discussion; a key may only delete its own thread if all replies also belong to that key. All changes require baseVersion. A repeated or stale action returns 409 without another mutation: read the draft to reconcile an uncertain outcome before submitting a new action. Comment-only changes preserve current approval and never change publication content. API keys need the separate draft:comment scope and are attributed to their key, never a human. Private social sets remain unavailable to keys.
